body.statement: As a required reduction, suppose exactly one hazard may depend on a substantive state: \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\). Then \(\mathsf C=1\) if and only if there are \(d<k\) and \(\ell\ge j\) with \(\ell\in B_d\). The minimal frontier consists exactly of the singleton designs \(B_d=\{\ell\}\) with all other bundles empty and \(d<k\le j\le\ell\).
body.justification: This arbitrary-horizon reduction forces the general calculus to reproduce a tractable boundary and its positive gamma-swap obstruction.
body.gap: The anchor proves passive nonidentification along a self-censoring path but does not state when a downstream audit destroys the cancellation or enumerate minimal audits.
body.consumer: It gives a closed-form measurement rule when scientific knowledge isolates one informative dropout hazard.

obligation.what_is_open: Only the translation of the complete single-hazard graphwise characterization from \(\operatorname{GID}\) to the undefined certificate value \(\mathsf C\) remains open.
obligation.obstruction: The causal identification boundary and positive countermodel are provable directly, but the statement is phrased in terms of \(\mathsf C\), so its final equivalence depends on the unresolved constructive-completeness theorem.
obligation.attempted: I derived an explicit recovery in both possible pre-hazard dropout regimes and built a positive arbitrary-alphabet countermodel by common survivor subdensity scaling, including a strictly positive Markov tail that transports the hidden marginal difference to the endpoint.
obligation.partial_result:
The following graphwise version of the claimed reduction is fully proved.
Condition throughout on a positive cell \((W=w,A=a)\).  Suppose that the
only continuation probability allowed to vary with the trajectory is
\(q_k(w,a,x_j)\), where
\(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\).  Then the endpoint law is
graphwise identified if and only if
\[
\tag{SH}
\text{there are }d<k\text{ and }\ell\ge j\text{ such that }\ell\in B_d.
\]

For sufficiency, assume (SH) and fix such \(d,\ell\).  Complete cases
identify the positive tail kernel
\[
L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z)
=\Pr(X_T=x\mid X_\ell=z,W=w,A=a,D=T),
\]
with the identity kernel used when \(\ell=T\).  Every response factor
after visit \(k\) is constant conditional on \((w,a)\), and the sole
nonconstant factor depends on \(X_j\), where \(j\le\ell\).  The
first-order Markov factorization therefore gives
\[
L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z)
=\Pr(X_T=x\mid X_\ell=z,W=w,A=a).
\tag{1}
\]
All denominators in this equality are positive by substantive and hazard
positivity.

If \(d\le k-2\), the event \(D=d\) only involves response probabilities
that are constant conditional on \((w,a)\).  It is therefore independent
of the substantive trajectory, and the audited table identifies
\[
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)
=\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=d)
=\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a).
\tag{2}
\]
If \(d=k-1\), the risk event \(D\ge k-1\) is independent of the
trajectory.  Put
\[
\rho_{w,a}
=\frac{\Pr(D\ge k\mid W=w,A=a)}
        {\Pr(D\ge k-1\mid W=w,A=a)}.
\]
The denominator is positive, and \(0<\rho_{w,a}<1\), by hazard
positivity.  Later response probabilities are constant, so the
distribution of \(X_\ell\) conditional on \(D\ge k\) equals its
distribution conditional on \(D=T\).  Partitioning the risk set according
to continuation at visit \(k\) yields the identified mixture
\[
\begin{aligned}
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)
={}&(1-\rho_{w,a})
 \Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=k-1)\\
&+\rho_{w,a}
 \Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=T)\\
=&\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The first conditional distribution in (3) is obtained from the audited
\(d=k-1\) table, and the second is routine in complete cases.  Equations
(1)--(3) give the evaluable reconstruction
\[
Q_a(x)=\sum_w p_W(w)\sum_{z\in\mathcal X_\ell}
       \pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z).
\tag{4}
\]

For necessity, suppose (SH) fails.  It is enough to construct the pair in
one treatment stratum and keep all other treatment strata, the positive
law of \(W\), and the positive treatment mechanism fixed.  Choose two
distinct strictly positive mass functions \(\mu,\mu'\) on
\(\mathcal X_j\).  Choose a positive vector \(c\) satisfying
\[
0<c(z)<\min\{\mu(z),\mu'(z)\}
\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal X_j.
\tag{5}
\]
Make \(X_1,\ldots,X_{j-1}\) mutually independent with common positive
laws in the two models.  In the first model let the conditional law of
\(X_j\), ignoring its allowed predecessor, be \(\mu\); in the second use
\(\mu'\).  Define the sole informative hazards by
\[
q_k(z)=\frac{c(z)}{\mu(z)},
\qquad
q'_k(z)=\frac{c(z)}{\mu'(z)}.
\tag{6}
\]
Condition (5) makes both hazards strictly between zero and one.  Take all
other hazards to be the same constants in \((0,1)\).

Choose common positive downstream transition kernels so that the two
endpoint marginals differ.  Such kernels exist for every specified finite
alphabet.  Explicitly, for each \(r\ge j\) choose a nonconstant function
\(h_r\) with \(\lvert h_r\rvert\le1\) and mean zero under a strictly
positive mass function \(\nu_r\).  Choose \(\mu,\mu'\) so that their
expectations of \(h_j\) differ, and, for \(r>j\), set
\[
K_r(y\mid z)=\nu_r(y)
 \{1+\lambda_r h_{r-1}(z)h_r(y)\},
\qquad 0<\lambda_r<1.
\tag{7}
\]
These are normalized strictly positive kernels.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb E\{h_r(X_r)\mid X_{r-1}=z\}
=\lambda_r h_{r-1}(z)
  \sum_y\nu_r(y)h_r(y)^2.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus the difference of the endpoint expectations of \(h_T\) is the
nonzero difference at visit \(j\), multiplied by strictly positive
factors.  If \(j=T\), the initial difference itself suffices.  Hence at
least one endpoint cell probability differs.

It remains to verify observational equivalence.  For every \(d\ge k\),
the full dropout subdensity is identical pointwise in the two models,
because the only changed product at visit \(j\) satisfies
\[
\mu(z)q_k(z)=c(z)=\mu'(z)q'_k(z).
\tag{9}
\]
For \(d\le k-2\), failure of (SH) implies that every coordinate in
\(I_d\) is strictly smaller than \(j\).  Those coordinates have the same
joint law in both models, and summing the changed suffix gives one, so
\(M_d=M'_d\).  For \(d=k-1\), the same observed-coordinate statement
holds, while marginalizing the failure factor at visit \(k\) gives in
both models
\[
\sum_z\{\mu(z)-c(z)\}
=1-\sum_zc(z)
=\sum_z\{\mu'(z)-c(z)\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Therefore all pattern tables agree.  Audit-table equivalence gives equal
laws of \(O\), whereas (8) gives unequal endpoint intervention laws.
Every substantive and response entry is strictly positive.  Independent
uniform disturbances realize the specified finite kernels, so the pair is
a legal causally sufficient Markovian SCM pair.  This proves necessity.

Consequently the inclusion-minimal graphwise-sufficient designs are
exactly those having one inclusion \(B_d=\{\ell\}\), all other bundles
empty, with \(d<k\le j\le\ell\).  Translating this proved characterization
from \(\operatorname{GID}\) to the frozen symbol \(\mathsf C\) requires
the still-open constructive-completeness theorem and is the only missing
step for the frozen proposition.
